status: prospective execution-method amendment before the next hosted measurement
scope: Hosted execution of the unchanged frozen main and laboratory studies at both CPU budgets

previous_method.description: One ubuntu-24.04 matrix job per CPU budget, each on its own hosted VM
previous_method.consequence: The 1-CPU shard's provenance/cpuinfo.txt names an AMD EPYC 9V74 with avx512f and the 2-CPU shard's an AMD EPYC 7763 without it, so the 1 versus 2 CPU difference mixed the budget with the host. Both shards' affinity.json select CPU 0 and CPUs 0,1, which share core_id 0 (thread_siblings_list 0-1).

reason: Within a budget all six arms already share one host. Running both budgets on the same VM removes the host from the budget comparison as well.
execution: One hosted job runs the controller with --cpus 1, uploads that shard, then runs it with --cpus 2 on the same VM, each with a fresh work and output directory. The order is fixed (1 then 2) and not randomized.

Each controller step has an 8,400 s wall budget under an 8,700 s outer timeout with a 480 s kill grace, inside a 155-minute step limit. Both steps together leave 50 of the job's 360 minutes for setup and uploads; release run 39810108196 needed 36 and 44 minutes for its two controller steps.
Before measuring, the 2-CPU controller refuses to start while an evaluation-owned container from the 1-CPU run is still running or an evaluation slice is still populated.

Each shard records provenance/host.json (boot ID, kernel release, first processor model and flags, sysfs topology of every allowed CPU) and control/host-lscpu-topology.stdout (lscpu CPU, CORE, SOCKET, CACHE and ONLINE columns) next to the existing affinity.json, cpuinfo.txt and lscpu record. Two shards whose budgets ran on one VM have byte-identical host.json records; neither the aggregate nor the report compares them.
unchanged: Both protocol files, the frozen corpus manifests, all input, reference and model bytes and their hashes.
Selection and bootstrap seeds, the seeded arm order within each budget, repetitions, first-attempt and scoring rules.
All six arms and their settings, the 1 and 2 CPU budgets, the selected logical CPUs, 3 GiB aggregate memory, zero swap and complete cgroup accounting.
The shard artifact names and layout, aggregate admission (identical candidate, bundle, evaluator and controller bytes) and the report inputs.
Candidate signature, attestation and executed-image identity admission.
interpretation: Report the host.json identity of both shards with any budget comparison. The 2-CPU budget remains the logical CPUs recorded in affinity.json, which on the hosted runners so far were two hardware threads of one core, and the fixed order means a budget difference also includes any drift between the two runs on that VM. Do not pool measurements made under this method with the separate-host measurement of run 39810108196.
